before.title: 12V auxiliary battery malfunction / drain
before.description: EQC owners report recurring 'Auxiliary Battery Malfunction' warnings, sometimes appearing repeatedly (every minute or so), along with dimming lights, intermittent infotainment glitches and occasional no-start. The small 12V auxiliary (AGM) battery that powers electronics weakens or its connections corrode/loosen; because EV electronics constantly draw on it, a marginal 12V battery causes a cascade of warnings. Resting voltage in the ~11.6V range indicates a failing battery.
before.solution: Check and clean/tighten the 12V auxiliary battery terminals first (loose/corroded connectors mimic a dead battery). If resting voltage is low (<12.2V) or faults persist after charging, replace the auxiliary battery with the correct AGM spec, then clear fault codes with a diagnostic tool. Typical replacement is inexpensive.
symptoms: Recurring 'Auxiliary Battery Malfunction' warning
Dimming lights
Intermittent infotainment/electronics glitches
Occasional no-start

before.title: Electric drive module coolant leak (motor reducer sealing)
before.description: Due to manufacturing deviations in the electric drive module, the internal cooling circuit can have insufficient sealing, causing coolant to leak — owners likened it to an EV 'oil leak.' If coolant enters the motor it can reduce the high-voltage system's insulation resistance over time; in extreme cases the drive module output power is reduced or the vehicle will not start. This triggered a very large China recall of 10,104 EQCs (later expanded to also cover EQA/EQB) for units built 30 Nov 2018 – 15 Dec 2021.
before.solution: Recall remedy: Mercedes service partners replace the affected electric drivetrain/drive module (a labor-intensive job, quoted up to ~18 hours). Owners outside China with leaks should have the drive unit inspected for coolant seepage under warranty.
symptoms: Coolant leak / fluid under vehicle
Reduced drive power / power limitation warning
Vehicle may not start in extreme cases
High-voltage / drive system warning

before.title: Electric power steering wiring harness water ingress / short circuit
before.description: The wiring harness for the electric power steering (steering control unit) can be damaged during the production process, allowing water/moisture into the harness. This can cause a short circuit and a sudden loss of electric power steering assistance, plus an increased fire risk. Affected EQC 400 4Matic units were built mainly in late 2019 to early 2020 (the DVSA/UK action cites Dec 2019–Mar 2020 build dates; the EU recall via car-recalls.eu is dated 13/02/2021 and a follow-up 06/12/2021). Mercedes issued multiple steering-related recall actions for the EQC.
before.solution: Recall remedy: dealer inspects the steering control unit wiring harness and replaces it if damaged, at no cost. Drivers get a red instrument-cluster warning before failure in many cases; the vehicle should be taken in immediately if shown.
symptoms: Loss of / heavier power steering assistance
Red steering warning in instrument cluster
Burning smell or fire risk
Steering fault message

before.title: Heavy cold-weather range loss and inefficient heat pump
before.description: EQC owners report large winter range drops — commonly 25-30%+ at around -10C, with real-world examples falling from ~230-239 miles to ~180-190 miles. While some cold-weather loss is normal for any EV, owners and reviewers single out the EQC's heat-pump/PTC heater strategy as relatively inefficient (the car leans on the energy-hungry PTC heaters rather than the heat pump), and the EQC lacks the flexible departure preconditioning of some rivals, making winter range management hands-on. Independent Norwegian cold testing measured ~25% loss.
before.solution: Not a defect with a single fix — mitigate by preculating/preconditioning the cabin and battery while plugged in, using seat/steering-wheel heating instead of cabin heat, and selecting eco/range modes. Some MBUX software updates improved heating logic; ensure the car is on current software. Verify the heat pump is functioning if losses are far beyond ~30%.
symptoms: Range drops 25-40% in cold weather
Reduced displayed range with heater on
Slow cabin warm-up
High energy consumption in winter

proposal.title: Heavy cold-weather range loss and inefficient heat pump

proposal.solution: Compare VIN-specific rated range with measured energy use, record ambient and battery temperature, speed, climate demand and preconditioning, and diagnose cabin-heating or battery-temperature faults separately. Do not buy a heat pump, compressor, heater or battery component from this page; no failed component or universal retail part is established.
symptoms: ambient and battery temperature recorded
energy use measured with climate demand documented
heating faults separated from expected cold-weather consumption

before.title: High-voltage battery housing corrosion from inadequate sealing
before.description: On early 2019-built EQC 400 4Matic vehicles, the high-voltage traction battery housing was not adequately corrosion-protected/sealed at the factory. Moisture can penetrate the housing and corrode internal components and electrical connections. In the worst case the vehicle cannot be restarted, and there is an elevated fire risk. This was a global recall (~1,463 units) and a separate but related EU recall (car-recalls.eu reference dated 09/07/2021).
before.solution: Mercedes recall remedy: dealer inspects the high-voltage battery housing and, where required, replaces the battery or applies corrosion-protection/sealing measures at no cost. Owners should run a VIN recall check before buying a used 2019 EQC and confirm the fix was performed.
symptoms: Vehicle will not start / cannot be restarted
High-voltage system warning
Corrosion or moisture in battery housing
Burning smell or fire risk in extreme cases

before.title: Inconsistent brake-by-wire pedal feel (regen/friction blending)
before.description: Owners widely report a non-linear, inconsistent brake pedal: 'spongy' or 'mushy' at the top of travel then suddenly 'grabby' lower down, making smooth stops hard. This stems from the EQC's brake-by-wire system blending regenerative and friction braking; the transition is not always seamless. Some owners also describe the system juddering or making a loud mechanical noise as the ABS/blending engages, and a different pedal feel on the first brake application after start-up. This is a recognized trait across Mercedes EQ models, not a one-off defect.
before.solution: Mercedes states some variation in pedal feel is normal for the brake-by-wire/regen system. Software updates have been applied to improve blending; persistent judder/noise should be diagnosed at a dealer (brake control unit / actuator checks). Owners can also adjust regen via the steering-wheel paddles to suit their driving.
symptoms: Spongy/mushy brake pedal at top of travel
Sudden grabby braking lower in pedal travel
Brake judder or loud mechanical noise during blending
Different pedal feel on first stop after start-up

citations.title: Mercedes EQC review: performance, motor & drive — DrivingElectric

proposal.title: Inconsistent brake-by-wire pedal feel (regen/friction blending)
proposal.description: The frozen page attributes inconsistent EQC pedal feel to a brake-by-wire regenerative/friction blending defect across every 2019-2023 vehicle. Manufacturer communication 10186135 includes one 2020 record for a single cracking noise from the ESP hydraulic unit after sharp braking without ABS intervention, not an inconsistent pedal-response defect. No exact government recall establishes the frozen identity or scope.
proposal.solution: Document pedal travel, deceleration, regeneration setting, battery state, speed, warnings and fault codes. If braking force or pedal response is abnormal, stop driving and obtain a qualified brake-system diagnosis. Do not buy brake, regeneration or hydraulic components from this page; no failed component or universal retail part is established.

battery state and regeneration setting documented
warnings and brake-system faults preserved

before.title: Side-impact crash sensor connector not latched (airbag/safety system fault)
before.description: The electrical connector of the side-impact (crash) sensors might not be correctly latched during assembly and could become detached. If the connection is lost, the side airbag/restraint deployment for that side may not function as intended in a crash, compromising occupant protection. EU recall via car-recalls.eu is dated 04/10/2021 and affects ~2020-build EQCs.
before.solution: Recall remedy: dealer inspects and correctly latches/secures the side crash sensor connectors (and replaces if needed) at no cost. An airbag/restraint warning lamp may illuminate if the connection has dropped.
symptoms: Airbag / SRS warning light
Restraint system fault message
Side airbag may not deploy in a crash
